title: Injection of Unicameral Bone Cysts with Bone Marrow Aspirate and Demineralized Bone Matrix Avoids Open Curettage and Bone Grafting in a Retrospective Cohort
authors: Kenneth R. Gundle; Etasha M. Bhatt; Stephanie E. Punt; Viviana Bompadre; Ernest U. Conrad
license: CC BY 4.0
scope: Retrospective cohort of 51 proximal humerus unicameral bone cysts treated with bone marrow aspirate and demineralized bone matrix injection; evidence is limited to this cohort and intervention.

title: Diagnosis and Current Treatment of Aneurysmal Bone Cysts
license: CC BY 4.0
scope: Narrative review of aneurysmal bone cyst diagnosis and treatment. Evidence summarizes literature and is not patient-specific; do not use as individualized treatment advice or as a substitute for current specialist guidance.

title: UK Guidelines for the Management of Bone Sarcomas
authors: Craig Gerrand; Fernanda Amary; Hanny A. Anwar; Bernadette Brennan; Palma Dileo; Maninder Singh Kalkat; Martin G. McCabe; Anna Louise McCullough; Michael C. Parry; Anish Patel; Beatrice M. Seddon; Jennifer M. Sherriff; Roberto Tirabosco; Sandra J. Strauss
publisher: British Journal of Cancer / British Sarcoma Group
license: CC BY 4.0
scope: UK consensus guideline for primary malignant bone tumours and giant-cell tumour of bone. Referral and MDT principles may inform pathway design; treatment/service recommendations reflect UK systems and must not be presented as universal or individualized advice.

title: Intraosseous Tumours of the Knee
authors: Luqman Wali; Ganesh Hegde; Michael Khoo; Ian Pressney; Lizz van der Heijden; Michael Bus; Roberto Tirabosco; Bhavin Upadhyay; Paul O'Donnell
license: CC BY 4.0
scope: Review of primary intraosseous tumours and tumour mimics identifiable on routine knee MRI, including subarticular and metaphyseal lesions. Anatomically restricted; imaging findings support differential diagnosis and do not establish an individual patient's diagnosis or treatment.

title: Conventional Radiography for the Assessment of Focal Bone Lesions of the Appendicular Skeleton: Fundamental Concepts in the Modern Imaging Era
authors: George R. Matcuk Jr.; Leah E. Waldman; Brandon K. K. Fields; Marco Colangeli; Marco Palmas; Alberto Righi; Giacomo Filonzi; Amandine Crombé; Paolo Spinnato
license: CC BY 4.0
scope: 2025 narrative imaging review of conventional radiography for focal appendicular bone lesions. Describes lesion location, multiplicity, density, margins, periosteal reaction, and matrix mineralization to inform differential diagnosis. Not an individualized diagnostic rule or treatment guideline; excludes use as standalone interpretation of patient images.

title: Society of Skeletal Radiology White Paper: Guidelines for the Diagnostic Management of Incidental Solitary Bone Lesions on CT and MRI in Adults (Bone-RADS)
authors: Connie Y. Chang; Hillary W. Garner; Shivani Ahlawat; Behrang Amini; Matthew D. Bucknor; Jonathan A. Flug; Iman Khodarahmi; Michael E. Mulligan; Jeffrey J. Peterson; Geoffrey M. Riley; Mohammad Samim; Santiago A. Lozano-Calderon; Jim S. Wu
publisher: Skeletal Radiology / Society of Skeletal Radiology
license: CC BY 4.0
scope: Society of Skeletal Radiology consensus white paper for incidental solitary bone lesions on CT and MRI in adults. The Bone-RADS algorithms are for diagnostic management, not definitive diagnosis, and do not cover multiple lesions or all patient populations. Clinical context and expert musculoskeletal radiologist judgment take precedence; not individualized advice or a standalone clinical rule.

title: Synovial Chondromatosis: A Narrative Review of Current Evidence on Diagnosis, Differential Diagnosis, and Management
authors: Hassan Zmerly; Luigi Di Lorenzo; Federica Dellafiore; Alberto Righi; Laura Campanacci
license: CC BY 4.0
scope: 2026 narrative review of synovial chondromatosis, including terminology, imaging, histopathology, differential diagnosis, recurrence, and management. Review authors state that evidence is largely case reports, retrospective series, and expert opinion; use for general educational retrieval only, not individualized diagnosis or treatment. The BTXRD label synovial osteochondroma is not assumed to be equivalent without annotation adjudication.

title: Osteofibrous dysplasia: a narrative review
authors: Rui Liu; Linjian Tong; Haiyang Wu; Qiang Guo; Lixia Xu; Zhiming Sun; Hua Yan
publisher: Journal of Orthopaedic Surgery and Research
license: CC BY 4.0
scope: Narrative review of osteofibrous dysplasia clinical features, imaging, pathology, terminology and management. Historical discussion of ossifying fibroma terminology is context only and does not define the BTXRD osteofibroma label or establish case-level equivalence. Use for general education, not individualized diagnosis or treatment.

title: Bone lesions of the tibia: Multimodal iconographic review and diagnostic algorithms, Part 1: Diagnostic algorithms, dysplasia and diaphyseal lesions
authors: Vincent Salmon; Pedro Augusto Gondim Teixeira; Alain Blum
license: CC BY 4.0
scope: Non-systematic narrative imaging review focused on tibial lesions, including OFD, differentiated adamantinoma and adamantinoma, plus dysplastic and other diaphyseal conditions. Multimodal educational context only; source descriptions/terminology and quoted frequencies require expert review and must not be treated as case-level BTXRD label mapping, standalone diagnosis, or individualized treatment advice.

title: Osteochondroma — NCI Dictionary of Cancer Terms
scope: NCI patient-facing glossary definition for general terminology only; not a clinical guideline and not a mapping for the BTXRD osteochondroma class label.
